segments: you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you you All right, good evening and welcome to the West Orange Board of Education public board meeting on Monday, January 27th, 2025. I would like to thank all of you here in person and those watching from home for joining us tonight. Ms. Flowers, please take the roll call. Good evening, everyone. Roll call, please. Dr. Bryant. Here. Mr. Stevenson. Here. Ms. Vera. Here. Vice President Ifker? Here. President Rock? Here. Thank you. Notice of meeting. The New Jersey Open Public Meetings Law was enacted to ensure the right of the public to have advance notice and to attend the meetings of public bodies at which any business affecting their interests are discussed or acted upon. In accordance with the provisions of the act, a written notice was sent from the office of the secretary of the board on January 7th, 2025. That said notice was sent by regular mail to the West Orange Township and the editors of the West Orange Chronicle and by email to the Star Ledger. That said notice was posted in the lobby of the administration building of the Board of Education and posted on the district website. Please be advised that this meeting is being recorded and may be broadcasted on local TV and the district's website at a future date. Please consideration of the closed and public meetings of December 16th, 2024, January 6th, 2025, and January 15th, 2025, do I have a motion to accept the minutes? So moved. Thank you, Mr. Stevenson. Is there a second? Second. Thank you, Mr. Ifker. Any comments? Hearing none. Just congratulations to those who were elected by the people of West Orange in November and sworn in on January 6th. So congratulations to my board colleagues. Oh, I'm sorry. Congratulations to the board colleagues who were elected in the recent November election. That's my only comment, President Rock, with respect to the minutes from January 6th of 2025. Thank you, Mr. Stevenson. Ms. Flowers, would you please take the welcome?

Dr. Bryant? Yes. Mr. Stephenson? Yes. Ms. Vera? Yes. Vice President Ifker? Yes. President Rock? Yes. Thank you. All right, next up we have our student liaison report from Nina Davis. Take it away. good evening last friday the west orange chinese club hosted their annual lunar new year celebration in the tarnaff cafeteria festivities included student cultural performances games a student art show and crafts a chinese dinner was provided for guests along with a raffle at the end of the night. Last Saturday, West Orange hosted the 19th annual West Orange High School Color Guard Invitational, where over 25 color guards from all over the East Coast were able to participate and showcase their amazing talent. On January 19th, the AB Salute Boys Step Team were the winners of the 18th annual Youth Step USA Brooklyn Borough Championship. So congratulations to them. To celebrate Black History Month, West Orange High School will be hosting a Black History Month dinner and celebration on February 13th. There will be local catering and festivities, including performances from the Boys and Girls Step Team, the Jubilee Choir, and the National Dance Honor Society. Tickets will soon be available for $15 each, and we hope to see you there. Thank you. Thank you for that, Nina. Next up, we have Mr. Moore. It is time for your report. Would you please share your superintendent's report with us at this time? Thank you, President Rock. One of our initiatives, my first initiative last year, was to bring air conditioning to our elementary classrooms. So we've completed our first phase of updating the electrical in the buildings, and it has been completed for Washington, Kelly, and St. Cloud. We will now begin to work on the electrical for Mount Pleasant, Gregory, Hazel, and Redwood. I will eventually call on our PTAs to rally behind a possible donation campaign so that we may help with the cost of effectively installing window units. Next, tonight we welcome Robert Haag of Lurch, Vinci, and Bliss. They're an auditing firm, and they will be presenting the comprehensive fiscal report.

Thank you, Robert. Thank you, board. Yeah, just a brief presentation tonight on your recently filed audit for the 23-24 fiscal year. Each year, every district in the state has to have an audit, external audit, and filed with the state of New Jersey Department of Education. What gets filed and what you have, what you receive from us is two books. One is a bigger book, which is the Comprehensive Annual Financial Report, which has all of your financial statements, our audit opinions, related note disclosures. Then you get a smaller report from us, which is the Orders Management Report, which discusses the results of the audit. Just to give you some highlights, in the big report, you receive three opinions from us, audit opinions. You receive what we call an unmodified opinion for all three of those opinions, basically the highest level of assurance an auditor can give. So you have one opinion on your financial statements on whether they're prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. Second opinion on your internal controls, which is more of looking at your processes and procedures, make sure there's no deficiencies in those internal controls. And then a third one is on your single audit, which relates to compliance with state and federal grant programs. So all three opinions, what we call our clean opinion, not a modified opinion. So very positive result of the audit on that front. Just to touch on some of the financials, the district closed the year from a surplus standpoint about 3.8 million dollars over the state minimum state maximum so the state only allows you to keep around two percent of your budget as unassigned fund balance which is really uh undesignated assigned surplus anything over and above that goes back into your budget in the next cycle so in your 25 26 budget you'll have 3.8 million dollars from savings from this budget to assist in that budget uh and that's pretty consistent to where you were last year at this time from from the june of 23 audit you had about

3.7 million dollars uh available for your 24 25 budget so you're kind of on equal footing from where you were last year as far as a fund balance standpoint so hopefully when you start preparing this budget at least you you know you're not in a shortfall to begin the budget process. You also have around total about $5.2 million in the capital reserve fund that's set aside for capital improvement purposes. $5 million of that is being used in the current budget. So of the $5.2, most of that is being used in the current or actually was budgeted in the current year budget. Anything that's not used in this budget will revert back into capital reserves. So you had 5.2 million of which, like I said, 5 million is budgeted. So once this year closes, whatever's not spent, that'll increase that 200,000. And that's available for future budgets or if the board at board discretion during the year, you could do a resolution to withdraw that money for any capital improvement purposes that's in your long range facilities plan. You also have around $2 million in a maintenance reserve fund. That's very similar to capital reserve, except it's for maintenance of your existing facilities. So it's not for major improvements or additions or alterations. It's really just for maintenance of your existing facilities. So something breaks, you could use that to fix it. You need to replace some equipment, you do that uh so it's more of a an ongoing maintenance rather than a long-term capital so all in all from from a financial standpoint you're you're pretty even from where you were last year so for a district your size to kind of keep that fund balance even is uh you know pretty stable financially um you know the only thing I would caution is and this is not specific to West Orange but uh you know you're using the money that you're saving from one year to assist with the budget in the next year. So that's a rolling process that you've been doing as

most districts do. So you just want to keep your eye on that. So if that tends to increase substantially, that could cause problems down the road, but you're not at that point yet. But just to caution you, as you're using that fund balance every year, you want to kind of maintain that same level each year. And from a management report standpoint, we did have six recommendations, which I believe there's a corrective action plan put in place that that'll be implemented to address those findings. We reviewed those with the business office. Of the six, none of them were what we call material or significant. They were all what we describe as general comments. So we start out at the general comment level, and if we deem it to be a significant deficiency in your internal controls, which caused that finding and recommendation, we would report that as a significant deficiency. Or if it's a material weakness that the finding caused a material weakness in your financial statements, we report that as such. But all six of these were what we call general comments so uh pretty easily correctable i think if that corrective action plan is implemented you know that hopefully they would be corrected going forward uh so all in all very positive audit on on the financial front and on on the recommendations front um so i'm happy to take any questions if anybody has any questions on either of those reports does the board have any questions one quick question yeah sure were any of the findings in the notes different from the findings of last year uh yes i think we had um there were six findings three of them did recur from last year uh so three of them were new three of them uh occurred again from last year um so i think we we talked about that there were kind of problems that are corrective actions being implemented. It hasn't been fully implemented yet. So that's why you see those correct, you know, the same findings again. So from

what we saw, it didn't look like, you know, nothing was done on those findings. It just looks like there needs to be continued improvement in those areas. But three of them were new ones ones three of them were repeats from the previous year mentioning the three that are repeats for everybody yeah sure um the one was um there's a level of uh charity bond that uh the treasurer has to maintain uh it's basically based on the size of your budget the state gives us a calculation to say based on the size of your budget here's the minimum bond charity bond that a treasurer has to maintain uh that was below the max, the state minimum. That could be the result. I don't have the detail in front of me, but that the, as your budget increases, the level of that surety bond has to increase. So potentially what could happen is we had that finding in last year's audit report. You were required to be at a certain level. You weren't last year. So we reported now this year, your budget went up again. So that minimum goes up again. So it could have been just really a calculation standpoint where I believe your bond may have been increased from last year, but now because your budget increased again, it's required to go up again. So although it's a repeat, like I said, it's kind of a continued corrective action. Another one was just on, you have some rolling pension and payroll related issues that for employees that are enrolled in the pension and require like a retro pay for salaries, there's pension associated with those retro salaries that have to be remitted to the state. So on a normal payroll basis, you withhold pension from your employees that gets remitted to the state as the payrolls occur. But when you have a retro that's owed for back pay, there's also pension associated with that. So what happens is there's a supplemental report that has to be filed for each quarter that that retro is

associated. So what has to happen is that those quarterly reports have to be filed to make up for all of those individual quarters. And then that pension would be remitted to the state. So again, I think that might've been a case of it was different retros in different years. So it's just a matter of keeping on top of when those retros are paid to make sure those supplemental pension reports and payments get remitted to the state. And the third one had to do with a capital asset appraisal. Each year, we have to report in your audit your value of all your capital assets, your buildings, your equipment, any machinery, and the related depreciation on that. So generally what happens is districts hire a third-party company to come in and do an appraisal. They'll update that appraisal and depreciation each year. So last year and this year, we didn't get the report. Last year, I believe we got the report after the audit was issued. This year, I think they were still in the process of preparing the report. So that's just a recommendation to say, you know, we need that report a little bit earlier because we need to report those numbers in the audit was issued this year, I think they were still in the process of preparing the report. So that's just a recommendation to say, let's, you know, we need that report a little bit earlier because we need to report those numbers in the audit. So I think what happened the last few years, the audit has been extended because of various reasons at the state level. So I think some of the third-party companies have got used to those extensions, but now the state is kind of reverting back to the original audit deadlines, which are a little bit earlier than it has been. So I think it's just a matter of keeping on top of them to get you that report as early as possible. Thank, thank you. All right. Thank you, Mr. Moore, for that for that report

next up do we have any committee reports or comments from the board sure i'll give a curriculum report um just a quick update on the status of the math interventions that are happening specifically in grades six through eight um there were district-wide classroom visits in october of 2024 and we have the results of those visits that make it clear about what we actually need to be working on in areas of focus for grades six through eight, also areas of support for our classroom teachers. What is encouraging is that we are focused on giving the students more of the cognitive load during the instructional time. We are focused on more opportunities for students to explain their learning and what they're understanding and more opportunities for students to discuss their learning with other students. So that feels very encouraging. Our next steps in this process, this week, our kids, if you have kids in the system, are taking diagnostics in their subjects. We will also have the results of classroom visits that will happen in February, focused on the discuss it portion of the classroom time. and we will have a report out to the curriculum committee that gives us progress on both math sort of where we are how things are going as well as the ELA implementation that started this past fall so excited to get those updates and as soon as we have them we will definitely share them here um that's it thank you for that dr bryant of course anything from you mr stevenson no sir thank you okay all right uh thank you for that committee report uh next up i would like to share my board president's report with you all recently one of our administrators was recognized by the west orange human relations Commission and was bestowed the 2025 Educator Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Award. Roosevelt Middle School Principal Lionel Hush was selected for this recognition for his commitment to

upholding the values of Dr. King through his exceptional service and dedication to making our schools more inclusive and more equitable. We salute Principal Hush and congratulate him on receiving this award. I also hear that our student liaison, Nina Davis, received an award there as well. So congratulations to you. That's all I have. Well, I'd also just like to say thank you for that report on the air conditioning. That is exciting to hear that we're moving forward with that. That's all I have. So next we will have questions from the public on agenda items only. Any community member who would like to make comments or ask questions, please come to the podium at this time. Please state your name and home address for the record and then begin your comments. Please limit your comments to three minutes. Do we have any members of the public here in the audience tonight who wish to make a public comment adam kramer tony moran road west orange i'm going to be commenting on some things i noticed from the audit report that are really policy questions that come from the audit report not that there are any problem with the audit itself the The first thing I noticed is if you look at Exhibit J4, in the fiscal year ending June 30, you had total revenues of just over a quarter billion dollars. $250,333,242. Your enrollment was 7,880. So if you do the math, you had a revenue stream of $35,357 in change per student. That figure is way more than double the national average. It is way more than the state average, and it's way more than the county average. My question is, with that much revenue, can we do things to help the taxpayer in terms of trimming the budget or making efficiencies so that the tax payers get a break without adversely impacting education. Numbers like that, I think there is some room for that. The next question I had related to total indebtedness of the town, county, and school board. Most people don't realize it.

Between our pro rata share of the town, county, and school board. Most people don't realize it, between our pro rata share of the county debt, the school board debt, and the town debt, there's over a quarter billion dollars in local debt out there. 256 million and change. Works out to about $21,000 a household. What are we gonna do to control the debt? Make sure we're using it wisely, paying it off, and getting the best possible interest rates because that's not sustainable for the town. In fairness, most of the debt's with the municipality, not you. The next question relates to things, and I think this is where you need a better interplay between the school and the town. The exhibit clearly shows that the top 10 property tax payers in the town dropped from 7.11 percent in 2015 to 5.4 last year meaning our commercial property base is shrinking that means school tax falls more and more on homeowners i'd like to know what you guys are doing with the town to make sure that they have land use policies, tax abatement policies that are not robbing your school revenues and then dumping it on the homeowner. Question four was about post-retirement. Wrap it up in a sentence or so. My last question relates to the $400,000 plus debt, bad debt that you have, and I want to know what's being done to collect it. It's mostly from school lunches. Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Kramer. Is there anybody else from the audience speaking on agenda items? Good evening, everybody. Margarita Sainz Soto. I live in Fort Brimont Road, very close to Redwood. I have a daughter who is in kindergarten in Redwood School, and I'm glad to hear that the AC units are moving forward, but I wanted to ask a little bit more about what's the timeline that we're looking at. It was an evening, it was September and it was very hot. So I can't imagine for five-year-olds, six-year-olds to be learning in that environment and I know that things are being done but I just want to get an idea of also from the parent side like what we do to support that because I'm just thinking when spring has come in and with climate change as you want to call it um the temperatures are going to be all over the place so that is that is my question. Thank you. Wait and see if anybody else. Is there anybody else for public comments at this time? Or Mr. Moore, would you like to touch on the air conditioning question? I'll talk budget for a second. No worries. In terms of the timeline for Redwood, we have to upgrade the electrical in Redwood, which puts us back a little bit longer. So you're looking at Redwood for 2026 in order to get that all online. Some of the all the schools were not sufficient as far as electrical um it was concerned so we had to upgrade every which is very expensive by the way because we're bringing electricity into the schools um and uh it took us a little time to budget because again we didn't do a referendum or anything of that nature we budgeted through our budget and uh so we had to do it in phases so um the first three schools as i mentioned i believe was right now that everything has been updated was kelly washington and saint cloud next is mount pleasant redwood hazelel, and Gregory. But I believe there are some, in order to upgrade the

So it will be coming because it's already been ordered for them, but it will take us a little bit of time to get everything online. Thank you, Mr. Moore. Thank you for the update. I can tell you that like last year, we explored different things, putting people in rooms, trying to combine things of that nature. We do have additional requests for staffing and professional development of things coming forward this year. And so we always have to balance what we need and what we want with what we can afford. And I'm sure that some of those things will have to get cut and some of those things will be in the budget. But we will be mindful of the total budget and the impact on the taxpayers as we go through that process. And with regards to debt, as you mentioned, the majority of that debt is the town debt. In my time on the board, I don't believe we've issued any new major debt. I will say that when I was elected, there was conversations about debt. People were talking about a referendum. I heard Mr. Moore just mention that we avoided that for two major reasons. One is facilities and the other is pre-K. So far, we've been able to expand pre-K without going out to a referendum. So we are, as a board, mindful of that, doing the best that we can to provide the best education with the best facilities and the best staff at a level that is, you know, as affordable as it can be for a place like Essex County.
